podcast.body: This album, featuring the cover of "Apache," became a seminal piece in early hip hop. "Apache" was a 1973 cover of a 1960 instrumental by British composer Jerry Lorton, and it quickly became known for its extended, minute-long percussion break. Music writer Michael Angelo Matos described the band's rendition as "the most crazed piece of orchestral funk ever recorded," maintaining the original's "noble and dramatic" shape while taking the liberty of extending the break with dueling trap drummer and congaist. This particular track is heavily sampled and considered the "national anthem of hip-hop." "Viner and his crew had concocted the most crazed piece of orchestral funk ever recorded."
